mainTopic: How a פרוסבול works and its land requirement, and which loans שביעית cancels: guaranteed documents and loans backed by a משכון
overview: The amud opens by finishing the explanation of the word פרוסבול. It protects both the rich (בולי) and the poor (בוטי), and a foreign speaker tells רבא that it means 'an arrangement of a matter.' שמואל rules that orphans need no פרוסבול, since the court is their father. A פרוסבול needs the borrower to own some land, even a tiny piece. The גמרא answers a challenge from הלל's pot with a hole, and shows that a guarantor's land, or the land of someone who owes the borrower, also works because of רבי נתן's rule. Next, רב and שמואל argue with רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש over whether שביעית cancels a שטר with a property guarantee. A story with רבי אסי shows that in practice רבי יוחנן rules that it is cancelled. Finally, the גמרא explains that a loan backed by a משכון is not cancelled because the lender acquires the משכון, as רבי יצחק learns from a פסוק. The amud ends by introducing another משנה from שביעית, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: בולי means the wealthy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that בולי, the first half of the word פרוסבול, refers to rich people, and supports this with a פסוק and a teaching of רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'בולי' means the wealthy. As the פסוק says, 'And I will break the pride of your power,' and רב יוסף taught that this refers to the wealthy people of יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing to explain the word פרוסבול by showing that 'בולי' means rich people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף reads 'the pride of your power' as the בולאות, the wealthy leaders of יהודה. So the word 'בולי' inside פרוסבול points to the rich lenders. The enactment protects them so their loans are not cancelled by שמיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: A document handing one's loans to the court so שמיטה does not cancel them

phrases.english: Bulei – these are the wealthy,
as it is written: “And I will break the pride of your power,”
and Rav Yosef taught:
these are the wealthy people of Judea.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of the name פרוסבול from the previous page.

steps.title: בוטי means the poor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that בוטי, the second half of the name, refers to poor people who need loans, based on a פסוק about lending.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'בוטי' means the poor, as the פסוק says, 'You shall surely lend him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining the name by showing that 'בוטי' means the poor borrowers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק's word for lending, הַעֲבֵט, is connected to 'בוטי,' the needy people who borrow. So the פרוסבול helps both sides: the rich keep their money safe, and the poor keep finding people willing to lend to them.
steps.whatToRemember: פרוסבול helps both the rich (בולי), whose loans are protected, and the poor (בוטי), who can still get loans before שמיטה.

phrases.english: Butei – these are the poor,
as it is written: “You shall surely lend him.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the pair started in step 1: after the rich, now the poor.

steps.title: רבא asks a foreigner what the word means
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks a foreign speaker for the meaning of the word פרוסבול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to a foreigner: What does 'פרוסבול' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks a foreign speaker what the word פרוסבול means. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since פרוסבול is a foreign word, רבא goes straight to someone who speaks that language. This offers a second explanation of the name, alongside the בולי and בוטי reading.

keyTerms.meaning: A foreigner, someone who speaks a foreign language

phrases.english: Rava said to a foreigner:
What is prosbol?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְלָעוֹזָא מַאי פְּרוֹסְבּוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different approach to the meaning of the word.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word פרוסבול in its original language.

steps.title: The foreigner explains: an arrangement of a matter
steps.stepSummary: The foreigner answers that פרוסבול means 'an enactment or arrangement of a matter.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It means an arrangement of a matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The foreigner answers רבא that the word means a formal arrangement or enactment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this reading, the name simply describes what the document is: an official enactment that sets up the loan so it can still be collected. It does not need the split into בולי and בוטי.

phrases.english: He said to him: the arrangement of a matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: פרוסבול means 'the arrangement of a matter.'

steps.title: Orphans do not need a פרוסבול
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל rules that orphans can collect their loans after שמיטה without a פרוסבול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: Orphans do not need a פרוסבול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a ruling that orphans are exempt from needing a פרוסבול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a lender needs a פרוסבול so שמיטה won't cancel his loans. שמואל says orphans who are owed money are protected even without one. The reason is given in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says that Shmuel says:
Orphans do not require a prosbol.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל יְתוֹמִין אֵין צְרִיכִין פְּרוֹסְבּוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the meaning of the word to a practical law about פרוסבול.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Orphans' loans are not cancelled by שמיטה even without a פרוסבול.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא supports it: the court is the orphans' father
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא teaches the same rule in a ברייתא and gives the reason: רבן גמליאל and his court act as the father of orphans.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so too רמי בר חמא taught: Orphans do not need a פרוסבול, because רבן גמליאל and his court are the father of orphans.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as שמואל and explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פרוסבול works by handing the loans to the court. With orphans, the court is already in charge of their affairs like a father, so their loans already count as being in the court's hands. That is why no document is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: And so too it was taught

steps.whatToRemember: Orphans don't need a פרוסבול because the court already looks after them like a father.

phrases.english: And similarly, Rami bar Ḥama taught:
Orphans do not require a prosbol,
because Rabban Gamliel and his court
are the father of orphans.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's ruling and supplies its reason.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that orphans do not need a פרוסבול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא taught by רמי בר חמא, which says the court is the father of orphans.

steps.title: A פרוסבול requires the borrower to own land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: a פרוסבול is written only if the borrower owns land; if he has none, the lender gives him a tiny piece of his own field.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה there: A פרוסבול is written only on land. If the borrower has none, the lender transfers to him any small amount of his own field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a משנה about the land requirement for a פרוסבול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פרוסבול needs the borrower to own some land. If he owns none, the lender can fix this by giving him even a tiny bit of his own field. The next steps ask how tiny that can be.

keyTerms.meaning: Any amount at all, even tiny

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in שביעית 10:6.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין כּוֹתְבִין פְּרוֹסְבּוּל אֶלָּא עַל הַקַּרְקַע.
phrases.english: One may write a prosbol only on land.
phrases.notes: He means the borrower has to own some land.

phrases.english: If he has none –
he transfers to him any amount within his field.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם אֵין כּוֹתְבִין פְּרוֹסְבּוּל אֶלָּא עַל הַקַּרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about what a פרוסבול needs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פרוסבול requires the borrower to own land; the lender may give him even a tiny bit.

steps.title: How small is 'any amount'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the smallest amount of land is that counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is 'any amount'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the minimum size of land that works. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said 'any amount,' which is unclear. The גמרא wants a real-world measure for the smallest piece of land that can be used.

phrases.english: And how much is any amount?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to define a term in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum amount of land that counts as 'any amount.'

steps.title: רב: even room for a cabbage stalk
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that even enough land to grow one cabbage stalk is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: Even enough for a cabbage stalk.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that a piece of land just big enough for one cabbage stalk is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows how tiny the land can be. As long as the borrower owns real ground, even a very small patch works.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi says that Rav says:
Even a stalk of cabbage.
phrases.notes: Meaning a patch of ground just big enough for one cabbage stalk to grow.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב אֲפִילּוּ קֶלַח שֶׁל כְּרוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even land big enough for one cabbage stalk counts.

steps.title: רב יהודה: even a lent spot for an oven
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה goes further: even if the lender only lent the borrower a spot for an oven and stove, a פרוסבול may be written.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Even if he lent him a place for an oven and a stove, a פרוסבול is written on that.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives an even more lenient ruling: a borrowed spot for an oven and stove is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the borrower does not even receive the land as a gift; he is only lent a place to use. Still, רב יהודה says this is enough for a פרוסבול, which goes beyond רב's cabbage stalk.

keyTerms.meaning: He lent him (for use, not as a gift)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 7: there the lender gives the land, but here he only lends a place to use.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says:
Even if he lent him a place
for an oven and a stove –
one writes a prosbol on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אֲפִילּוּ הִשְׁאִילוֹ מָקוֹם לְתַנּוּר וּלְכִירַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an even more lenient case after רב's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a borrowed place for an oven and stove is enough for a פרוסבול.

steps.title: Challenge from הלל: only a pot with a hole counts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the lenient rulings from a teaching of הלל: a פרוסבול is written only on a pot with a hole, not on a pot without one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But הלל taught: A פרוסבול is written only on a pot with a hole. A pot with a hole, yes; a pot without a hole, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the lenient rulings by quoting הלל, who seems to demand something truly connected to the ground. The next step finishes the challenge, and step 13 gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pot with a hole counts like land because it draws from the ground below, but a pot without a hole does not. If even a pot without a hole is not enough, it seems hard to accept that a mere borrowed oven spot is enough. The next step sharpens this challenge, and step 13 answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: A flowerpot with a hole in it

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't Hillel teach:
One does not write a prosbol
except on a perforated pot alone.
Perforated – yes,
not perforated – no;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the lenient minimums just stated.
steps.kashyaTarget: The lenient rulings about the minimum needed for a פרוסבול, especially רב יהודה's borrowed oven spot.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: הלל requires something that truly counts as land and rules out a pot without a hole, which seems to clash with accepting a mere borrowed spot.

steps.title: Why doesn't the pot's spot count as land?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sharpens its challenge: if even an oven's spot is enough land for רב יהודה, an unperforated pot also sits on a spot of land.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not? There is its place!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge it started in the last step. It asks why הלל says an unperforated pot doesn't work, since the pot is sitting on a spot of ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה said even the spot of an oven and stove is enough land for a פרוסבול. By that logic, the ground under any pot should be enough, whether or not the pot has a hole. So הלל's rule seems to contradict רב יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: its place, the spot it rests on

phrases.english: Why? But there is its place!
phrases.notes: "Its place" is the spot of ground under the pot, just like the oven's spot in step 10.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge from step 11 by spelling out why הלל's rule clashes with רב יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's ruling that an oven's spot is enough land, as it relates to הלל's pot rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every pot rests on some ground. If any spot of ground counts, an unperforated pot should work too, yet הלל says it doesn't.

steps.title: The pot is resting on stakes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that הלל is talking about a pot resting on stakes, so it isn't sitting on the ground at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where it rests on stakes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. הלל means a pot raised up on stakes, so there is no ground 'under it' that the borrower is using.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the pot is off the ground, there is no spot of land involved. The only question left is whether the pot itself counts as land. A pot with a hole counts as land, and a pot with no hole does not. רב יהודה's oven case is different, because the oven really sits on the ground.

keyTerms.meaning: it is only needed for (this case): the rule is talking about a specific situation

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where it is resting on stakes.
phrases.notes: So the pot isn't touching the ground. Only a pot with a hole counts as land in that case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by narrowing הלל's case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed הלל's pot was sitting on the ground, so its spot should count as land.
steps.terutzMaskana: הלל means a pot raised on stakes. Only a pot with a hole counts as land there, so there is no contradiction with רב יהודה.
steps.whatToRemember: Even a tiny spot of land works for a פרוסבול. הלל's pot rule is about a pot that isn't touching the ground at all.

steps.title: רב אשי gave borrowers a palm stump
steps.stepSummary: In practice, רב אשי gave the borrower ownership of a palm-tree stump so he could write a פרוסבול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי would transfer to him a palm-tree stump and write a פרוסבול on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us what רב אשי actually did. To make a borrower a landowner, he gave him a palm stump, then wrote a פרוסבול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This puts the earlier rule into practice: the lender may give the borrower a small piece of land. A stump still rooted in the ground counts as land. It is a tiny, nearly worthless piece of land, but that is enough.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi would transfer to him
a stump of a palm tree,
and he wrote a prosbol on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי מַקְנֵי לֵיהּ גִּידְמָא דְּדִיקְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life example of the minimal-land rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Giving the borrower a palm stump that is still rooted in the ground is enough land for a פרוסבול.

steps.title: רב אשי's students handed debts to each other
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of רב אשי's yeshiva protected their loans by handing them over to one another.
steps.simpleTranslation: The scholars of רב אשי's yeshiva would hand over their matters to each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports another method. The scholars in רב אשי's yeshiva handed their debts over to each other instead of writing a פרוסבול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמיטה cancels debts that are owed to a person. It does not cancel debts handed over to a בית דין. By handing the debt to colleagues who acted as a court, the scholars kept their loans from being cancelled.

phrases.english: The Sages of the school of Rav Ashi
would hand over their matters to each other.
phrases.notes: "Matters" means their debts. They handed them over to colleagues acting as a court, so שמיטה wouldn't cancel them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן דְּבֵי רַב אָשֵׁי מָסְרִי מִילַּיְיהוּ לַהֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from writing a פרוסבול to a simpler method of handing debts over.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Handing a debt over to colleagues acting as a court protects it from שמיטה.

steps.title: Is a verbal handover enough? Yes
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן handed a debt over to רבי חייא בר אבא, asked if anything more was needed, and was told no.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן handed over a matter to רבי חייא בר אבא. He asked: Do I need anything else? He answered: You don't.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story confirming the handover method. רבי חייא בר אבא tells רבי יונתן that simply handing the debt over is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יונתן wondered whether he also needed a written document or some formal act. The answer was no: the handover by itself protects the debt from שמיטה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan handed over matters
to Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba;
he said to him: Do I need anything else?
He said to him: You do not need.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן מְסַר מִילֵּי לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the handover method from step 15 with a story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A simple handover of the debt is enough; nothing more is required.
steps.whatToRemember: Besides writing a פרוסבול, a lender can protect his loan by handing the debt over to a court, and that handover alone is enough.

steps.title: Using the guarantor's land
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if the borrower has no land but the guarantor does, a פרוסבול can be written.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If he has no land but the guarantor has land, a פרוסבול is written on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that widens the land requirement. The guarantor's land is good enough for a פרוסבול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the borrower himself had to own land. Here we learn that land owned by the ערב (guarantor) also works, since the lender can collect from him.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לוֹ קַרְקַע, וְלֶעָרֵב יֵשׁ לוֹ קַרְקַע –
phrases.english: If he has no land, but the guarantor has land –
one writes a prosbol on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין לוֹ קַרְקַע, וְלֶעָרֵב יֵשׁ לוֹ קַרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the land requirement and widens it to include the guarantor.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The guarantor's land is enough for a פרוסבול.

steps.title: Using the land of someone who owes the borrower
steps.stepSummary: If neither the borrower nor the guarantor has land, the land of someone who owes the borrower money is enough. This is based on רבי נתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he and the guarantor have no land, but someone who owes him has land, a פרוסבול is written on it, based on רבי נתן.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes one step further: the land of the borrower's own debtor works too. The גמרא says this comes from רבי נתן, setting up the source in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lender could, in a sense, collect from the borrower's debtor. So that person's land counts as backing the loan. The words 'from רבי נתן' signal that a source is coming.

keyTerms.meaning: the one who owes him (the borrower's debtor)
based on the view of רבי נתן

phrases.english: If he and the guarantor have no land,
but the one who owes him has land –
one writes a prosbol on it,
based on Rabbi Natan –

steps.triggerLanguage: לוֹ וְלֶעָרֵב אֵין לָהֶן קַרְקַע, וְלַחַיָּיב לוֹ יֵשׁ לוֹ קַרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the ברייתא's rule from the guarantor to the borrower's debtor.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The land of someone who owes the borrower money is enough for a פרוסבול.

steps.title: רבי נתן: collect directly from the debtor's debtor
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן learns from a פסוק that if A lent to B and B lent to C, the court can collect from C and pay A directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught: רבי נתן says: From where do we know that if one lends his friend a מנה, and that friend lends his friend, we take from this one and give to that one? The verse says: 'And give it to the one he is guilty toward.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי נתן's teaching as the source for the last rule. Money can go straight from the second debtor to the first lender.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק tells the thief to give the money to whoever it really belongs to. רבי נתן learns from this that the money can skip the middleman. That is why the land of the borrower's debtor counts as backing the original loan.

keyTerms.meaning: the lender, the one who is owed

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Natan says:
From where is it derived for one who lends his friend a maneh,
and his friend lends to his friend,
from where that we take from this one and give to that one?
phrases.notes: The court takes from the last borrower and pays the first lender, skipping the middleman.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"And he shall give to the one he is guilty toward."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind 'from רבי נתן' in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the land of the borrower's debtor can support a פרוסבול
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי נתן's ברייתא learning from במדבר 5:7 that a court collects directly from a debtor's debtor
steps.whyThisMatters: רבי נתן's principle, known as שעבודא דרבי נתן, is a major rule in monetary law. It shows that a debt can reach past the middleman.
steps.whatToRemember: A פרוסבול can rest on the borrower's land, the guarantor's land, or even the land of someone who owes the borrower money, thanks to רבי נתן's rule.

steps.title: The משנה: the seventh year cancels loans with or without a document
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from מסכת שביעית: שביעית cancels loans, whether they were made with a שטר or without one.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה there: The seventh year cancels a loan, whether it was made with a document or without a document.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a משנה about שמיטת כספים. It is setting up a disagreement about what the משנה's words mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses two phrases: 'בשטר' (with a document) and 'שלא בשטר' (without a document). The next steps argue over exactly which kinds of loans each phrase covers.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh year, the שמיטה year

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in שביעית 10:1.

phrases.english: The seventh year cancels the loan,
whether with a document or without a document.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the laws of פרוסבול to the related question of which loans שביעית cancels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שביעית cancels loans made both with a שטר and without a שטר.

steps.title: רב and שמואל: even a guaranteed document is cancelled
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל explain that 'with a שטר' means a שטר with אחריות נכסים, and 'without a שטר' means a שטר without it. An oral loan is surely cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל both say: 'With a document' means a document that has a property guarantee. 'Without a document' means a document that has no property guarantee. And certainly an oral loan is cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: רב and שמואל give their reading of the משנה. In their view, שביעית cancels every kind of loan, even one backed by a property guarantee.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They read 'בשטר' as the strongest kind of loan, a שטר with a property guarantee. 'שלא בשטר' then means a weaker שטר with no guarantee. An oral loan is not even mentioned, since if strong documents are cancelled, an oral loan surely is.

keyTerms.meaning: A property guarantee: the borrower's land is pledged to pay the loan
An oral loan, with no document

phrases.english: It is Rav and Shmuel who both say:

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁטָר – שְׁטָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ אַחְרָיוּת נְכָסִים,
phrases.english: "With a document" means a document that has a property guarantee,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא בִּשְׁטָר – שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אַחְרָיוּת נְכָסִים;
phrases.english: "without a document" means one that has no property guarantee;
all the more so an oral loan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Interprets the two phrases of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שביעית cancels even a שטר with אחריות נכסים.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש: a guaranteed document is not cancelled
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש explain that 'with a שטר' means a שטר without a property guarantee, and 'without a שטר' means an oral loan. A שטר with אחריות נכסים is not cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and רבי שמעון בן לקיש both say: 'With a document' means a document that has no property guarantee. 'Without a document' means an oral loan. But a document that has a property guarantee is not cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: A second pair of אמוראים reads the same משנה differently. For them, a loan backed by a property guarantee survives שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here each phrase is moved one level down: 'בשטר' is a plain שטר, and 'שלא בשטר' is an oral loan. That leaves the guaranteed שטר outside the משנה, so it is not cancelled. This is the direct opposite of רב and שמואל.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish who both say:

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁטָר – שְׁטָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אַחְרָיוּת נְכָסִים,
phrases.english: "With a document" means a document that has no property guarantee,
"without a document" means an oral loan.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שְׁטָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ אַחְרָיוּת נְכָסִים – אֵינוֹ מְשַׁמֵּט.
phrases.english: But a document that has a property guarantee is not cancelled.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reading of the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שביעית does not cancel a שטר with אחריות נכסים.
steps.whatToRemember: רב and שמואל say a guaranteed שטר IS cancelled by שביעית. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש say it is NOT cancelled.
steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree a plain שטר and an oral loan are cancelled. The only argument is about a שטר with a property guarantee.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a loan document is cancelled, but if it has a property guarantee it is not cancelled. This matches רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that matches רבי יוחנן and רבי שמעון בן לקיש: A loan document is cancelled, but if it has a property guarantee, it is not cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא openly separates a plain שטר חוב, which is cancelled, from one with אחריות נכסים, which is not. That is the same line רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש drew.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught in agreement with him

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא כְּוָתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish:
A loan document is cancelled,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם יֵשׁ בּוֹ אַחְרָיוּת נְכָסִים – אֵינוֹ מְשַׁמֵּט.
phrases.english: but if it has a property guarantee, it is not cancelled.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּוָתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the view in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: The view of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש that a guaranteed שטר is not cancelled.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that says a שטר with אחריות נכסים is not cancelled.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: even a general guarantee protects the loan
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא says that if the borrower set aside one field for the loan, it is not cancelled. Even if he only wrote that all his property guarantees the loan, it is still not cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: If he set aside one field for his loan, it is not cancelled. And not only that, but even if he wrote 'All my property is pledged and guaranteed to you,' it is not cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that also says a guaranteed loan survives שביעית, and it goes further.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first case is a specific field set aside for the loan. The 'ולא עוד' adds a bigger point: even a general guarantee on all his property, with no specific field named, is enough to keep the loan from being cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but even

phrases.english: It is taught in another baraita:
If he set aside for him one field for his loan,
it is not cancelled.
And not only that, but even if he wrote:
"All my property is pledged and guaranteed to you"
it is not cancelled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second supporting ברייתא that extends the rule.
steps.raayaObject: The view that a guaranteed loan is not cancelled.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that says both a specified field and a general guarantee on all property prevent cancellation.

steps.title: רבי אסי rules a guaranteed document is not cancelled
steps.stepSummary: A relative of רבי אסי had a שטר with a property guarantee. He asked רבי אסי if שביעית cancels it, and רבי אסי said no.
steps.simpleTranslation: A relative of רבי אסי had a document with a property guarantee written in it. He came to רבי אסי and asked: Is it cancelled or not? He told him: It is not cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a real case. רבי אסי rules like רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, that a guaranteed שטר survives שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is exactly the case argued over above: a שטר with אחריות נכסים. רבי אסי's answer fits what רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש taught.

phrases.aramaic: קָרִיבֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַסִּי הֲוָה לֵיהּ הָהוּא שְׁטָרָא
phrases.english: A relative of Rabbi Asi had a certain document
that had a property guarantee written in it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַסִּי, אֲמַר לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: He came before Rabbi Asi and said to him:
Is it cancelled or is it not cancelled?
He said to him: It is not cancelled.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָרִיבֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַסִּי הֲוָה לֵיהּ הָהוּא שְׁטָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A practical case that applies the ruling of step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אסי rules that a שטר with אחריות נכסים is not cancelled by שביעית.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן tells the same man that it is cancelled
steps.stepSummary: The relative left רבי אסי and asked רבי יוחנן, who said the guaranteed שטר IS cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: He left him and came before רבי יוחנן, who said to him: It is cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues with a surprise: רבי יוחנן rules that the guaranteed שטר is cancelled. This sets up a question the גמרא will deal with next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 22, רבי יוחנן himself said a guaranteed שטר is NOT cancelled. Now he rules that it IS cancelled. This clash with his own view is what the גמרא needs to explain.

phrases.english: He left him and came before Rabbi Yoḥanan,
who said to him: It is cancelled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story with a ruling that seems to go against רבי יוחנן's own view in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן rules that this guaranteed שטר is cancelled.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't miss the problem: this is the same רבי יוחנן who said in step 22 that a guaranteed שטר is NOT cancelled. The גמרא will need to explain this.

steps.title: רבי אסי asks רבי יוחנן directly
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי comes to רבי יוחנן and asks whether שביעית cancels a שטר that has a property guarantee.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי came before רבי יוחנן and said to him: Does it cancel the loan or not?
steps.whatsHappening: After hearing that his relative got a different answer, רבי אסי goes to his teacher רבי יוחנן to ask the question himself. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אסי had ruled 'not cancelled,' and he believed this followed רבי יוחנן's own teaching (step 22). Now he wants to hear רבי יוחנן's ruling firsthand.

keyTerms.meaning: before him, in front of him

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא רַבִּי אַסִּי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi came before Rabbi Yochanan,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מְשַׁמֵּט אוֹ אֵינוֹ מְשַׁמֵּט?
phrases.english: he said to him: Does it cancel, or does it not cancel?
phrases.notes: He's asking about the same case: a שטר that has a property guarantee.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתָא רַבִּי אַסִּי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the relative's conflicting answers from רבי אסי and רבי יוחנן
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether שביעית cancels a שטר with אחריות נכסים

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rules that it is cancelled
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that שביעית does cancel the guaranteed שטר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It cancels.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a clear ruling: the debt is cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches what he told the relative in step 26. It seems to go against the explanation from step 22, which the next step points out.

phrases.english: He said to him: It cancels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אסי's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שביעית cancels even a שטר with אחריות נכסים

steps.title: But you yourself said it is not cancelled
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי challenges רבי יוחנן: wasn't it you who said a guaranteed שטר is not cancelled?
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it the Master himself who said it does not cancel?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי points out that רבי יוחנן seems to be contradicting his own earlier teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 22, רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש explained that a שטר with אחריות נכסים is not cancelled. Now רבי יוחנן rules the opposite, so רבי אסי asks how both can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: the Master (a polite way to say 'you')

phrases.english: But wasn't it the Master who said
it does not cancel!
phrases.notes: He's pointing back to רבי יוחנן's own explanation in step 22.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling just given
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the guaranteed שטר is cancelled
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It contradicts his own earlier statement that a שטר with אחריות נכסים is not cancelled

steps.title: A theory is not a practical ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers: just because we reason that way in learning, should we actually act on it?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Just because we reason this way, should we carry out an action based on it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains that his earlier statement was a line of reasoning in learning, not a ruling to follow in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not take back the reasoning itself. He says it is not strong enough to rely on in practice, so the actual ruling is that the debt is cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: we compare, reason, think it through
carry out an action, rule in practice

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying his earlier statement was wrong in theory. He is saying it does not become the practical הלכה.

phrases.english: He said to him:
And just because we reason this way,
should we carry out an action?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָנוּ מְדַמִּין, נַעֲשֶׂה מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The earlier statement was a practical ruling
steps.terutzMaskana: The earlier statement was only reasoning; in practice the debt is cancelled

steps.title: But a ברייתא agrees with you
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי pushes back: there is a ברייתא that supports the earlier view.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא like the Master's view?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי argues that the earlier view is more than a theory, because a ברייתא says it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He means the ברייתא from step 23: a שטר with a property guarantee is not cancelled. If a ברייתא says so, why not act on it?

phrases.english: He said to him: But isn't it taught in a baraita in agreement with the Master!
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא from step 23.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'only theory' answer
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the earlier view is only reasoning
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא supports it, so it should be followed in practice

steps.title: That ברייתא may follow בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the ברייתא might follow בית שמאי, who hold that a שטר ready to be collected counts as already collected.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Perhaps that ברייתא follows בית שמאי, who say: A שטר that stands to be collected is considered as already collected.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן takes away the force of the ברייתא by saying it may follow a view we do not rule like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי think a guaranteed שטר is as good as paid, so there is no open debt left for שביעית to cancel. Since the הלכה does not follow בית שמאי here, the ברייתא does not decide the practical ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: a document that stands to be collected

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, רבי יוחנן rules that שביעית cancels even a שטר with אחריות נכסים. The ברייתא saying otherwise may follow בית שמאי.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דִּלְמָא הָהִיא בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הִיא,
phrases.english: He said to him: Perhaps that one is Beit Shammai,
who say:
A document that stands to be collected is considered as already collected.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns aside the ברייתא brought as support
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The ברייתא's power to set the practical הלכה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may follow בית שמאי, whose view is not accepted here

steps.title: משנה: loans with a משכון or given over to court are not cancelled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in שביעית: a loan backed by a משכון, and שטרות handed to בית דין, are not cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: One who lends his friend money with a משכון, and one who hands his שטרות over to בית דין, these debts are not cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a משנה about two cases that שביעית does not cancel. This sets up the question that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two cases are listed together: a loan with a משכון, and the פרוזבול-like case of giving one's שטרות to בית דין. Both escape cancellation.

keyTerms.meaning: collateral, an item held as security for a loan
one who hands his loan documents to the court

phrases.english: We learned there:

phrases.aramaic: הַמַּלְוֶה אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ מָעוֹת עַל הַמַּשְׁכּוֹן,
phrases.english: One who lends his friend money with a collateral,
and one who hands his documents over to court,
they are not cancelled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic within the laws of שביעית
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Loans with a משכון, and שטרות handed to בית דין, are not cancelled by שביעית

steps.title: Why is a loan with a משכון not cancelled?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא understands the court case, since the court holds the documents, but asks the reason for the משכון case.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for one who hands his שטרות to בית דין, because the court holds them. But a loan with a משכון, what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the reason for the first case and asks for the reason behind the second case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When בית דין holds the documents, the court is the one collecting, and שביעית only stops a private lender from demanding payment. With a משכון, no court is involved, so the reason is not clear.

phrases.english: It makes sense for one who hands his documents to court,
since the court holds them.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מַלְוֶה עַל הַמַּשְׁכּוֹן, מַאי טַעְמָא?
phrases.english: But one who lends with a collateral, what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind part of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a loan backed by a משכון is not cancelled by שביעית

steps.title: רבא: because the lender holds it
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the lender is already holding something of the borrower's.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Because he has seized it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a reason: the lender has the borrower's item in his hands, so the debt is not cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's first answer is based on physical holding: since the lender holds the item, it is as if he already has payment.

phrases.english: Rava said: Because he has seized it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The lender holds the משכון, so the debt is not cancelled

steps.title: אביי: then living in the borrower's courtyard should work too
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא: if holding is enough, a lender who lives in the borrower's courtyard also holds something, so his loan should not be cancelled either.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, if he lent him money and lives in his courtyard, he holds it, so should that also not be cancelled?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tests רבא's reason with another case and shows it leads to a result that cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Living in the borrower's courtyard is also a way of holding his property. If holding alone protected a loan, this loan would be safe too, but אביי assumes it is cancelled. So 'holding' cannot be the full reason.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: If that is so,
if he lent him and lives in his courtyard, since he holds it,
would it also not be cancelled?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's reason
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reason that holding the item prevents cancellation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Living in the borrower's courtyard is also holding, yet that loan is cancelled

steps.title: A משכון is different: the lender acquires it
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that a משכון is different because the lender actually acquires it, as learned from רבי יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A משכון is different, because he acquires it, as we learn from רבי יצחק.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא makes his reason sharper: it is not just holding, but real ownership of the משכון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Living in a courtyard is only use, not ownership. With a משכון the lender gets a real ownership right, so the debt counts as collected. The source for this comes in the next step.

phrases.english: He said to him: Collateral is different,
since he acquires it, as we learn from Rabbi Yitzchak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any physical holding of the borrower's property prevents cancellation
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a משכון, which the lender legally acquires, prevents cancellation

steps.title: רבי יצחק: the פסוק shows a lender acquires the משכון
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק learns from 'וּלְךָ תִּהְיֶה צְדָקָה' that a lender acquires a משכון; otherwise returning it would not be called צדקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: From where do we know a lender acquires a משכון? As it says 'And it shall be צדקה for you.' If he does not acquire it, what צדקה is there? From here we learn a lender acquires a משכון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רבא's claim that a lender owns the משכון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה calls returning the משכון to the poor borrower 'צדקה.' Giving back something that is not yours is not charity, so the lender must own the משכון. This supports רבא's answer.
steps.whatToRemember: A loan with a משכון is not cancelled by שביעית because the lender acquires the משכון, as רבי יצחק learns from 'וּלְךָ תִּהְיֶה צְדָקָה.'
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that a lender owns the משכון explains why this case is different from a lender who only uses the borrower's property.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yitzchak said:
From where do we know that a creditor acquires the collateral?
As it says: "And it shall be righteousness for you."
phrases.notes: דברים 24:13, about returning the poor man's משכון to him at night.

phrases.english: If he does not acquire it, where is the righteousness?
From here we learn that a creditor acquires the collateral.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: מִנַּיִן לְבַעַל חוֹב שֶׁקּוֹנֶה מַשְׁכּוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבא's answer
steps.raayaObject: That a lender acquires the משכון
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק 'וּלְךָ תִּהְיֶה צְדָקָה' (דברים 24:13), as explained by רבי יצחק

steps.title: Introducing a משנה from another place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new section by announcing that it will quote a משנה taught in a different מסכת.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה there:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It tells us that a משנה from another מסכת is about to be quoted, but the quote itself has not come yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words תְּנַן הָתָם are a standard opening formula. They tell us the coming source is a משנה with full authority, and that it comes from a different מסכת than the one we are learning. The discussion of רבי יצחק and משכון is finished, and a new topic is starting.

keyTerms.meaning: 'There' — in a different מסכת, not the one we are learning now

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for a ruling in this line. It is only an announcement, and the actual משנה comes right after it.

phrases.english: We learned there:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the discussion of רבי יצחק's proof about משכון and opens a new section by bringing a משנה from elsewhere.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This line only introduces a משנה that will be quoted next.
